# OpenDeviceRouter

> Session router for coding agents and test runners. Allocates an iOS Simulator, Android emulator or cloud device from the user's own machine, a free GitHub runner, or a device cloud the user has an account with (Appetize, Revyl, Limrun, AWS Device Farm). Installs a build, waits for the first usable screenshot, exposes screenshot, tap, type, swipe and key input, releases the device on every exit path, verifies closure, and writes a versioned receipt. Free-only routing by default. MIT. Pre-release 0.1.0, install from GitHub.

- Repository: https://github.com/QA-army/open-device-router
- Install: `git clone https://github.com/QA-army/open-device-router && cd open-device-router && npm install && npm run build && npm link && npm i agent-device`
- Check setup: `odr doctor`
- Keys for every provider (signup URL, key location, env var, gh secret line): `odr keys --all` or docs/keys.md
- Run a session around a command: `odr run --platform android --build app.apk --minutes 10 -- <cmd>` (exit 0 ok, 3 refused, 4 failed, 5 closure unverified)
- SDK: `import { allocate, withSession, attach } from "opendevicerouter"`; Midscene: `import { midsceneInterface } from "opendevicerouter/midscene"`
- Clean up dead sessions: `odr sweep`

## Rules

- The user signs up with each provider; odr never creates accounts or accepts terms.
- odr never stores credential values.
- Do not quote benchmark numbers that are not in bench/RESULTS.md.
